summary: This page is the cover of the SGX REIT annual report, serving as a table of contents that lists all sections and their corresponding page numbers without containing any specific financial tables, audited portfolio data, or distribution highlights. no schema-relevant data

This page presents the **Key Figures for 2025** of Keppel DC REIT, featuring a main table of financial highlights including Distributable Income of \$268.1m, Aggregate Leverage of 35.3%, Assets under Management of \$6.3b, Distribution Per Unit (DPU) of 10.381 cts, and Portfolio Occupancy of 95.8%. The reporting unit is consistently stated in SGD millions or cents where applicable.

This page of the Keppel DC REIT annual report features a "Momentum" section highlighting record financial performance, including a Total Unitholder Return of 317.0% and Distribution Per Unit (DPU) of 10.381 cts for the year ended 31 December 2025. It details key metrics such as Distributable Income of $268.1 million, Assets Under Management of $6.3 billion, and portfolio occupancy of 95.8%, alongside strategic acquisitions and growth initiatives without presenting audited Portfolio Statements, P&L tables, or tenant mix data.

This page presents the Group Financial Highlights for SGX REIT, featuring a table of Results Highlights and Ratios with gross revenue ($441,362 '000) and distribution per unit (DPU) data alongside Balance Sheet Highlights and Ratios showing investment properties and unitholders' funds in SGD'000. The content also includes a Half-Yearly Results breakdown comparing First Half and Second Half performance against the Full Year figures.

This page of the Keppel DC REIT annual report presents a Board Composition Dashboard featuring tables detailing board tenure, gender diversity, independence, age profile, and meeting attendance for FY 2025. The content outlines governance policies aligned with the Monetary Authority of Singapore's Code of Corporate Governance 2018 and describes risk management frameworks without including any audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant mix data.

This page presents the Trust and Organisation Structure diagram of Keppel DC REIT alongside its organizational hierarchy, detailing relationships between Unitholders, The Trustee (Perpetual (Asia) Limited), and The Manager (Keppel DC REIT Management Pte. Ltd.) without any financial statements or data-extraction schema-relevant tables.

This page details Keppel DC REIT's 10th Annual General Meeting held on 15 April 2025 and lists accolades, memberships, research coverage, unitholding by geography (Singapore 21.4%, North America 18.1%, Asia excluding Singapore 9.4%, UK 6.5%, Europe excluding UK 6.0%, Others 38.6%), and unitholding by type (Sponsor and related parties 19.2%, Institutional 45.9%, Retail 34.9%) as at 4 February 2026.

This page presents Unit Price Performance data for Keppel DC REIT, featuring a monthly trading performance table and chart reporting SGD'000 volume and USD per Unit closing prices from January to December 2025, alongside comparative yield tables in SGD'000 showing a distribution yield of 4.6% against various indices.

This page presents Keppel DC REIT's global data centre portfolio as of 31 December 2025, highlighting $6.3 billion in assets under management across 25 facilities in 10 countries via a world map and a detailed asset list. The content explicitly names the reporting unit as USD billions (noted as \$6.3b) and lists specific property valuations including locations such as Keppel DC Dublin 1, Almere Data Centre, and Tokyo Data Centre 1, but contains no audited financial statements, tenant tables, or distribution highlights.

This page presents data centre market analysis for Guangdong (using Guangzhou as a proxy) and Tokyo, Japan, featuring the main artifact "Guangzhou Data Centre Supply/Demand/Utilisation" table with IT Capacity (MW) and Utilisation Rate (%) projections from 2025E to 2029F alongside a corresponding chart. The second primary artifact is the "Tokyo Data Centre Supply/Demand/Utilisation" table detailing Total Live Supply, Total Take-up, and Utilisation Rate trends over the same period, accompanied by descriptive notes on market dynamics such as cloud provider strategies and regulatory constraints but contains no audited financial statements or tenant-specific revenue data.

This page presents an independent market review of data centre landscapes in Amsterdam, Eindhoven, and Cardiff, featuring a bar-and-line chart titled "EINDHOVEN DATA CENTRE SUPPLY/DEMAND/UTILISATION" displaying Eindhoven's stable 2025E through 2029F metrics. The text details supply/demand dynamics, key players like Switch Datacenters and Microsoft, and policy impacts across these Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets without including any audited portfolio statements, financial tables, or specific reporting unit schemas (e.g., SGD'000).

This page presents supply/demand/utilisation tables for Cardiff and London data centre markets from 2025E to 2029F, reporting metrics in MW and % without a specified monetary reporting unit. The Cardiff table shows Total Live Supply and Take-up rising from 124 MW to 293 MW with utilisation at 99.7%, while the London table indicates supply increasing from 1,548 MW to 2,443 MW with utilisation climbing from 92.2% to 96.9%.

This page features a glossary of data centre assets and strategic updates on 2025 acquisitions including Tokyo DC 3 (valued at JPY 83.0 billion) and full ownership of KDC SGP 7 and 8, alongside divestments such as Kelsterbach DC to Fortinet GmbH for EUR 50.0 million. The main artifact highlights that Assets Under Management reached SGD 6.3 billion, representing a 26% year-on-year increase, with 84.5% of the portfolio located in Asia Pacific.

This page presents the **TOTAL ATTRIBUTABLE LETTABLE AREA BY GEOGRAPHY (%)** and **PORTFOLIO AUM BY GEOGRAPHY (%)** tables as at 31 December 2025, detailing Singapore's dominance in lettable area (27.4%) versus its majority share of AUM (62.4%), alongside text describing portfolio composition, tenant mix strategies, lease expiries, and specific asset management activities such as land tenure extensions and value uplift from operational efficiencies.

This page presents the Weighted Average Lease Expiry (WALE) by contract type, the Portfolio Contract Expiry Profile by Lettable Area and Rental Income for Keppel DC REIT as at 31 December 2025. The data tables detail WALE figures of 3.2 years for Fully-fitted (Colocation), 9.6 years for Fully-fitted (Single Tenant), and 6.1 years for Shell and Core assets, alongside expiry distributions across years 2026 to ≥2031 categorized by lettable area percentages and rental income percentages.

This page presents a Portfolio Review featuring two donut charts detailing rental income breakdown by contract type (Fully-fitted Colocation 72.7%, Fully-fitted Single Tenant 21.2%, Shell and Core 6.1%) and client trade sector (Internet Enterprise 69.3%), alongside a Top-N tenants table listing ten anonymous Fortune Global 500 companies and providers contributing over 81% of rental income as at 31 December 2025, followed by portfolio statistics including total attributable lettable area of 2,721,198 sq ft and valuation of S$6.07 billion reported in SGD'000s.

This page presents the **Statement of Portfolio (property valuations)** for Keppel DC REIT's Asia Pacific assets, displaying a table with five data centres (Keppel DC Singapore 1–5) that includes their locations, ownership interests, gross floor areas, occupancy rates, attributable lettable areas, and financial metrics such as **attributable gross revenue** (S$ million), purchase prices, and independent valuations as at 31 December 2025.

This page presents the **At A Glance** portfolio review for Keppel DC REIT's Asia Pacific assets, detailing five data centre facilities (Keppel DC Singapore 7/8, DC1, Gore Hill Data Centre, and Guangdong Data Centre 1) with metrics in **S$ million**. The table displays key attributes including land area, gross floor area, lettable area, client counts, lease types, occupancy rates, facility managers, purchase prices, and independent valuations as of 31 December 2025.

This page presents a detailed asset table for five data centre properties (Guangdong Data Centre 2, Guangdong Data Centre 3, Tokyo Data Centre 1, Tokyo Data Centre 3, and Basis Bay Data Centre) reporting attributable lettable area in sq ft, occupancy rates, and Attributable Gross Revenue in S$ million. The table includes specific financial metrics such as purchase price and valuation in S$ million alongside foreign currency equivalents (RMB, JPY, RM), facility managers, lease types, and ownership percentages, with footnotes clarifying the basis of valuations, divestment announcements, and shared land areas.

This page presents a "Portfolio Review" featuring a detailed **Statement of Portfolio (property valuations)** table that lists five data centres across Europe, including their locations, ownership interests, land and floor areas, occupancy rates, attributable gross revenue in SGD'000, purchase prices, and independent valuations as at 31 December 2025. The report explicitly names the reporting unit as SGD'000 for revenue figures while providing dual currency values (SGD and EUR) for purchase price and valuation metrics.

This page presents a Statement of Portfolio detailing the physical attributes, ownership, and financial metrics for five SGX REIT data centre assets located in the Netherlands and United Kingdom. The reporting unit is SGD'000 (denoted as S$ million), with attributable gross revenue figures listed as S\$3.5 million through S\$5.5 million per facility.

This page of the Keppel DC REIT FY 2025 annual report primarily features a **Gross Revenue table** (in SGD million) detailing revenue breakdowns by asset type for 2025 ($441.4m total) and 2024 ($310.3m total), alongside supporting text on Distributable Income, Distribution Per Unit (DPU), and Net Property Income.

This page presents the **GROUP FINANCIAL OVERVIEW** table for Keppel DC REIT, detailing FY 2025 financial highlights including gross revenue of SGD'000 441,362, net property income of SGD'000 383,260, and profit attributable to Unitholders of SGD'000 427,820. The report also includes a Distribution Policy section confirming that at least 90.0% of distributable income is distributed on a half-yearly basis.

The page presents an Investment Properties and Investment Property Held for Sale table detailing the carrying value breakdown of 23 specific data centre assets across global locations as at 31 December 2025, with a total portfolio value of \$6,150.5 million (SGD'000) compared to \$4,920.5 million in 2024. Additionally, it includes text sections on Net Asset Value per Unit and Cash Flows and Liquidity, reporting cash equivalents of \$336.5 million and operating cash flows of \$262.8 million for FY 2025.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for Keppel DC REIT features a Debt Maturity Profile (%) table and Key Statistics as at 31 December, reporting aggregate leverage at SGD'000 (35.3% in 2025), an interest coverage ratio of 7.5 times, and total borrowings of SGD'000 2,375.6 million. The content also includes funding details such as new green financing facilities totaling SGD'000 1,344.0 million, unutilised facilities of SGD'000 774.3 million, and proceeds from a preferential offering of SGD'000 398.9 million.

This page details the utilisation of net proceeds as at 31 December 2025 and February 2026, outlines capital management policies including compliance with the Property Funds Appendix of the CIS Code (aggregate leverage below 50.0% of deposited properties), and presents financial highlights in SGD'000 showing Distributable Income of \$268.1 million and a Distribution Per Unit of 10.381 cts for the year ended 31 December 2025.

This page of the Keppel DC REIT sustainability report (FY 2025, March 2026) presents a table listing entities and assets within the reporting scope, including KDC SGP 1–8, Gore Hill DC, Basis Bay DC, and Dublin data centres. The reporting unit is SGD'000 for financial alignment but this specific page contains no audited Portfolio Statement, revenue/expense tables, tenant mix, or DPU highlights; it instead details ESG standards (IFRS S1/S2, GRI 2021), internal assurance by DNV Business Assurance Singapore Pte. Ltd., and contact information at investor.relations@keppeldcreit.com.

This page presents the **ESG Targets and Commitments table** for Keppel DC REIT, detailing nine selected UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with associated short-, medium-, and long-term targets alongside FY 2025 performance metrics such as Scope 1 and 2 emissions (38,538 tCO₂e), water withdrawal (714.6 ML), green financing share (25.6%), and corporate governance rankings. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated in the text, but the data aligns with standard SGX REIT sustainability disclosures covering environmental stewardship, responsible business, and sustainable finance.

This page presents a table detailing ESG factors, UN SDGs, targets, and FY 2025 performance across categories including Employee Health and Wellbeing, Human Capital Management, and Community Development. The content further outlines MSCI ESG Ratings (AA), GRESB Green Star designation, industry affiliations such as LIEN and REITAS, and signatory statuses for the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact and PRI Principles.

This page details the SGX REIT's sustainability approach, including an audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) with building characteristics and asset values inclusive of land value, alongside external data sources from ClimSystems' Climate Insights and country-specific historical climate/weather data. It outlines key assumptions such as no changes in portfolio assets or implementation of mitigations, limitations regarding post-assessment acquisitions, and presents selected NGFS scenarios (Disorderly, Orderly, Hot House World) within a Transition Risks versus Physical Risks matrix diagram.

This page presents Keppel DC REIT's performance and progress on emissions, featuring a "TOTAL SCOPE 1 AND 2 GHG EMISSIONS (tCO2e)" table with values in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. The document details the refined GHG emissions methodology for 2025, including Scope 3 indirect emissions totaling 201,029 tCO2e, alongside initiatives for energy efficiency and climate action policies.

This page presents the Qualitative Physical Risk Assessment Results for Keppel DC REIT in a table format, detailing five key physical risks (Extreme Precipitation, Extreme Water Level, Mean Sea Level Rise, Extreme Temperature, and Heat Wave Days) across short, medium, and long-term horizons with corresponding business impacts and responses. The reporting unit is not explicitly shown in this text segment.

This page presents a Qualitative Transition Risks and Opportunities Assessment table detailing regulatory, market, and reputation risks such as increasing carbon prices and enhanced reporting obligations, along with Keppel DC REIT's corresponding business responses. The content focuses on risk descriptions, time horizons (short, medium, long term), and mitigation strategies without containing any of the specified schema-relevant data artifacts like audited portfolio statements or financial highlights.

This page presents a table of climate-related transition opportunities for Keppel DC REIT, detailing business impacts and responses such as cost savings from energy-efficient technology, increased access to green capital (including the 2025 Green Financing Framework), government incentives, and shifting stakeholder expectations. The section further outlines quantitative analysis results using NGFS scenarios for 2024–2030 and reports specific financial figures, including approximately S$9.69 million in capital expenditures for transformer upgrades and S$280,000 incurred in 2025 for green certificates, though no audited portfolio statements or tenant tables are present.

This page details Keppel DC REIT's environmental stewardship, including climate transition planning and water management performance across its Singapore properties. The key artifact is the Total Water Withdrawal table reporting 2023–2025 figures in ML (megalitres), showing a 50.4% year-on-year increase to 714.6 ML in 2025 driven by new acquisitions, alongside metrics for NEWater usage and water consumption intensity.

This page details Keppel DC REIT's nature and biodiversity stewardship efforts, specifically the 2024 LEAP assessment of its data centre portfolio (including KDC SGP 7) which identified low to medium risks for all sites. The content outlines key nature-related dependencies such as water scarcity, flood damage, and noise pollution alongside corresponding mitigation responses and external tools used for evaluation.

This page presents IFRS S2 disclosure requirements for climate-related targets and provides Keppel DC REIT's industry-based metrics on energy consumption (45.6% coverage, 2,053,859 GJ consumed), water management (45.6% coverage, 714.6 ML withdrawn), tenant sustainability impacts (88.5% separately metered for electricity), and asset details including 25 total assets with 95.8% portfolio occupancy. All data is reported in the units specified within the table (e.g., GJ, ML, sqm, percentages).

This page serves as the Table of Contents for the SGX REIT annual report, listing all financial statements including the audited Portfolio Statement (page 115) and Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss (page 108), alongside governance sections on pages 164 and 191. This page contains the Independent Auditor's Report to the Unitholders of Keppel DC REIT, confirming that the Group's consolidated financial statements and Trust-specific statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 are properly drawn up in accordance with Singapore Financial Reporting Standards (International) and applicable CIS Code requirements. The report outlines the scope of the audit, including the audited portfolio statement as at that date, but does not present any specific tables or data artifacts such as audited portfolio values, revenue figures, DPU, or manager information.

This page details the Key Audit Matter regarding the valuation of investment properties, confirming that as at 31 December 2025, the Group's investment properties carried at fair values of SGD'000 amounted to approximately 89.4% of total assets with specific disclosures referenced in Notes 4(i), 4(ii), and Note 29. The audit procedures focused on assessing the competence of independent valuers and the reasonableness of key inputs such as capitalisation rates and discount rates against industry standards.
This page presents the Statements of Financial Position for the SGX REIT Group and Trust as at 31 December 2025, reporting assets, liabilities, net assets, and unitholders' funds in SGD'000.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss for SGX REIT, reporting financial highlights in SGD'000 including gross revenue ($441,362k), property expenses, management fees, finance costs, fair-value changes, and tax. The statement details profit before tax of $472,719k and profit after tax attributable to unitholders of $427,820k, alongside earnings per unit figures.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting Group profit after tax of $434,682 and total comprehensive income attributable to unitholders of $426,292 (in SGD'000), alongside other comprehensive loss components including currency translation movements and hedging reserve adjustments.

This page presents the **Statement of Movements in Unitholders' Funds** for SGX REIT, detailing the year-end balance as of 31 December 2025 and comparative figures for 2024 in SGD'000. The table tracks changes in Units in Issue, various reserve accounts (Foreign Currency Translation, Hedging, Other), Accumulated Profits, Unitholders' Funds, Non-Controlling Interests, and Total equity through operations, other comprehensive income, and unitholder transactions including distributions and capital contributions.

This page presents the Statement of Total Return for the SGX REIT Trust, reporting Unitholders' Funds in SGD'000 for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024. It details profit after tax (72,733 SGD'000 for 2025; 175,926 SGD'000 for 2024), distributions to unitholders, management fee payments, and net asset changes resulting from both operations and unitholder transactions.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting cash flows from operating activities (net cash from operations: $262,829), investing activities (net cash used: $(1,125,603)), and financing activities (net cash generated: $886,460) in SGD'000. The table details specific line items including acquisitions of interests in investment properties ($1,165,437), proceeds from issuance of Units ($489,460), distributions paid to Unitholders ($203,994), and the resulting net increase in cash and cash equivalents of $23,686.

This page presents the **Reconciliation of Liabilities Arising from Financing Activities** for Keppel DC REIT, detailing year-end balances and movements in borrowings, lease liabilities, and interest payable for 2025 and 2024 in SGD'000. The table explicitly lists additions, interest expense, and currency translation differences to reconcile opening balances at 1 January with closing balances at 31 December for each liability category.

This page presents the Distribution Statement for the year ended 31 December 2025, detailing the amount available for distribution to Unitholders ($SGD'000) and specific distributions made during the period. The table includes a breakdown of net tax and other adjustments in Note A, listing items such as trustee's fees, rental income adjustments, fair-value changes, management fees, and foreign exchange gains/losses.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for SGX REIT as of 31 December 2025, detailing investment properties across multiple locations with their land tenure, lease terms, carrying amounts at fair value reported in SGD'000, and percentage of total net assets. The table includes specific data centres such as Guangdong DC 1, Tokyo DC 3, and maincubes DC under both fully-fitted and shell-and-core categories, alongside notes indicating that accompanying notes form an integral part of the financial statements.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement as at 31 December 2025, listing investment properties including Keppel DC Singapore facilities, Gore Hill DC in Australia, and Basis Bay DC in Malaysia with their locations, land tenure, lease terms, remaining lease durations, carrying amounts at fair value in SGD'000, and percentages of total net assets. The statement details a total investment property value of SGD 6,150,492'000 alongside notes receivables and other assets/liabilities to arrive at total net assets of SGD 4,230,116'000.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for investment properties, detailing the Group and Trust carrying amounts at 1 January and 31 December 2025 alongside movements including acquisitions, additions, divestments, capital expenditure, net fair value changes, and currency translation differences, all reported in SGD'000. The section further reconciles these figures to valuation reports by adding lease liabilities to derive the final carrying amount and describes the fair value measurement methodologies employed by independent valuers such as Savills and JLL.

This page details the Group's investment property and asset held for sale activities, featuring a Statement of Investment Property Held for Sale table (GROUP, 2025: $17,092 '000) and a Statement of Asset Held for Sale table (GROUP AND TRUST, 2025: $75,426 '000). It further includes narrative disclosures on land lease extensions, divestments of Basis Bay DC and Kelsterbach DC, and the transfer of NetCo Bonds to assets held for sale.

This page presents the Investment in Subsidiaries table and a listing of significant subsidiaries for Keppel DC REIT, reporting values in $'000. The primary artifact details the cost less accumulated impairment of investments at 31 December 2025 ($3,867,223) alongside capital injections, impairments, and reversals, while the subsidiary list identifies entities such as Keppel DC REIT Fin. Company Pte. Ltd., Memphis 1 Pte. Ltd., and Datacentre One LLP with their principal activities, places of incorporation, and effective equity percentages held by the Trust for both 2025 and 2024.

This page presents the **audited Portfolio Statement** detailing the Trust's subsidiaries, including their principal activities, places of incorporation, and effective equity held percentages for 2025 and 2024, alongside a table of loans to subsidiaries reported in SGD'000.

This page details the Group's investment in M1 Network Private Limited ("NetCo") via a summarised statement of financial position and a summarised statement of comprehensive income for 2024, reporting figures in $'000. The tables present NetCo's net liabilities of $(32,651) and its total comprehensive loss of $(31,761), including revenue of $50,900, finance costs of $(18,131), and depreciation and amortisation of $(37,536).

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Notes Receivables and Trade and Other Receivables, detailing balances in SGD'000 for Group and Trust segments as of 2025 and 2024. The notes provide specific details on AU DC Note subscription terms and NetCo Bonds reclassified to asset held for sale, along with accruals for unbilled lease income and amounts due from subsidiaries.

This page contains the Derivative Financial Instruments table for SGX REIT, detailing notional amounts and fair values of forward exchange contracts and interest rate swaps designated as cash-flow hedges for the years ended 31 December 2024 and 2025 in SGD'000. The data distinguishes between current and non-current maturities (2026–2031) and reports assets and liabilities for both hedging and non-hedging derivatives across the group.

This page presents a derivatives table detailing the maturity, notional amounts, and fair value impacts of forward exchange contracts and interest rate swaps for the SGX REIT trust as of 2025 and 2024. The data shows that interest rate swaps are designated as cash flow hedges to mitigate floating rate risks on borrowings, while non-designated forward contracts aim to reduce foreign currency risk, with associated net fair value losses recorded in the hedging reserve.

This page contains the audited Portfolio Statement of Derivative Financial Instruments detailing the Group's hedging strategy for 2025 and 2024, including notional amounts, carrying values, and maturity dates for interest rate and foreign exchange hedges reported in SGD'000. Additionally, it presents a Statement of Deposits showing the write-off of fully impaired deposits related to the Guangdong DC 3 acquisition as of 31 December 2025, also valued in SGD'000.

This page presents the Deferred Taxation table detailing the Group's and Trust's deferred tax assets and liabilities (reported in SGD'000) arising from investment properties, tax losses carried forward, and allowances against assets for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024. It further includes a movement schedule of temporary differences recognized in profit or loss and other comprehensive income, alongside an explanation that net amounts are determined by offsetting related assets and liabilities within the same entities.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for Cash and Cash Equivalents (Note 13) and Loans from Subsidiaries (Note 14), detailing Group and Trust balances in SGD'000 for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, alongside a table of loans and borrowings (Note 15) showing non-current and current liabilities including capitalised transaction costs and lease liabilities.

This page presents the debt repayment schedule and terms for Group borrowings, detailing interest rates ranging from 1.51% to 4.78% per annum with maturities between 2026 and 2031, alongside a Statement of Trade and Other Payables and Provision for Taxation reported in SGD'000. The tables disclose face values and carrying amounts for liabilities, categorized by group and trust, including specific notes on other payables such as deferred payments, management fees, and accrued development costs.
